statement: For a filtered inner join over Study 01's 200,000-donation fixture, five alternative spellings (JOIN ... ON with the filter, a filtered derived table, a CTE naming the filtered input, a CTE naming the joined rows, and a comma join) ran the same plan as JOIN ... WHERE in all 120 spelling, selectivity, engine and phase pairs: selectivity 0.01% to 90%, PostgreSQL btree and YugabyteDB range index, isolated and blended phases, three runs each. The 27 pairs whose sign agreed across runs had identical plans, magnitudes of 0.2-40% and directions that changed between phases, so no difference is attributable to the spelling.

statement: Forcing MATERIALIZED on a CTE that contains the join, with the selective filter applied outside it, multiplied the query time against the same CTE left to the engine. On PostgreSQL the factor was 84-101x at 0.01% selectivity, 51-64x at 0.1% and 23-27x at 1%, falling to 1.02-1.44x at 90%. On YugabyteDB with a range index it was 34-49x, 20-29x and 8.1-9.5x, falling to 0.93-1.03x at 90%. Three runs per engine and phase. With the filter inside the CTE, forcing MATERIALIZED cost at most 1.61x on PostgreSQL and 0.71-1.25x on YugabyteDB.
limits: the penalty is plan-explained on both engines (the materialization boundary keeps the outside filter from reaching the join), measured as end-to-end latency of one reader
YugabyteDB at 90% is inside its position drift (0.93-1.03x), so no reversal is claimed
with a hash-sharded YugabyteDB index the same hint looked nearly free (earlier runs: 1.4-1.7x) because there was no selective path to lose; this claim holds for the range-index arm

statement: For one expensive CTE referenced n times, NOT MATERIALIZED against MATERIALIZED crossed between one and two references on PostgreSQL at the unselective (100%) consumer and on YugabyteDB at both consumers. At n=2 NOT MATERIALIZED took 1.43-2.06x the MATERIALIZED time and at n=16 3.9-12.1x, in every run of both phases. At n=1 the ratio was 0.81-0.94 on YugabyteDB at the 1% consumer (6 of 6 runs) and 0.87-1.07 at the 100% consumers. Both engines' default policy ran MATERIALIZED's plan from two references.
limits: the YugabyteDB one-reference advantage at the 1% consumer is small (6-19%) but has the same sign in all six runs
the n=1 point at the 100% consumers is mixed in sign, so the crossing is bracketed between 1 and 2 references, not located

statement: On a 3-node YugabyteDB cluster (RF3, 2 CPU/3 GiB per node), pre-splitting the joined relations into three tablets, with leaders gated onto three nodes, changed join times against the single-tablet layout in every run. A 2,000-row join took 0.73x (isolated) and 0.71x (blended), and a 180,000-row join 0.54x and 0.71x. The 20-row join was 1.22x slower in the isolated phase and unresolved in the blended phase. At 180,000 rows the split layout was also 0.71-0.76x the single node and the equal-total single node.
limits: the nodes are containers on one laptop, so this is data placement without a network
tablet count and leader spread change together in this pair; a split single-node arm was not run
the 1 CPU client was throttled in 32-46% of its CFS periods in every run; point reads are the most exposed
placement was verified by yb_table_properties and yb-admin leader listings before and after each distributed run
